learning_outcomes.text: Students must demonstrate possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts regarding the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: THERMODYNAMICS

Topic 1: TEMPERATURE AND HEAT: Basic concepts. Zeroth principle of thermodynamics. Concept of temperature and thermometric scales. Types of thermometers. Equations of state of a system. Thermal coefficients. Heat. Heat capacity and specific heat. Phase changes: latent heat.
Topic 2: FIRST PRINCIPLE OF THERMODYNAMICS: Thermodynamic work. Internal energy. Statements of the first principle. Thermodynamic transformations of an ideal gas.

Topic 3: SECOND PRINCIPLE OF THERMODYNAMICS: Necessity of the second principle. Statements of the second principle. Carnot cycle and theorem. Thermodynamic temperature scale. Clausius theorem. Entropy. Entropy variations of an ideal gas.
BLOCK II: ELECTROMAGNETISM

Topic 4: ELECTRIC FIELD AND POTENTIAL: Electric charge. Coulomb's Law. Electric field. Electric flux. Gauss's Law: applications. Potential difference. Electric potential. Calculation of electric potential. Electrostatic potential energy.

Topic 5: ELECTRIC FIELD IN MATTER: Conductors and insulators. Conductors in electrostatic equilibrium. Capacitance of a conductor. Capacitors and capacitance. Energy stored in a capacitor. Electric dipole in an external field. Capacitors with dielectric.

Topic 6: ELECTRIC CURRENT AND DC CIRCUITS: Electric current: intensity and current density. Resistance and Ohm's Law. Energy in electric circuits: electromotive force and batteries. Analysis of DC circuits. RC circuits: charging and discharging of a capacitor. Measuring instruments: galvanometer, ammeter, and voltmeter.

Topic 7: THE MAGNETIC FIELD AND ITS SOURCES: Introduction. Magnetic field lines. Magnetic flux. Motion of charged particles in a magnetic field. Force on a conductor. Hall effect. Torques on current loops. Magnetic field created by a moving charge. Magnetic field created by electric currents: Biot-Savart Law. Ampere's Law: applications.
Topic 8: ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION: Introduction. Electromotive force due to motion. Faraday's Law. Lenz's Law. Mutual inductance. Self-induction. Magnetic energy. RL circuits. Magnetism in matter.

Topic 9: ALTERNATING CURRENT: Introduction. Elementary alternator. Sinusoidal electromotive force. Series RLC circuit. Average and RMS values. Ohm's Law applied to RMS quantities. Power in alternating current circuits. The transformer.

Topic 10: ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES: Introduction. The wave equation for electric and magnetic fields. Electromagnetic waves. Intensity of an electromagnetic wave. Emission of electromagnetic waves. The electromagnetic spectrum.
Practical work: Calibration of a thermometer
Practical work: Specific heat of a solid
Practical work: Equation of state of ideal gases
Practical work: Electric field and potential between the plates of a capacitor
Practical work: Ohm's Law. Resistor association
Practical work: Charging and discharging of a capacitor
Practical work: Magnetic field in coils and solenoids
Practical work: Resonance in RLC circuits: Tuner circuit

assessment_methods.method: Participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities

assessment_rules: To pass the theoretical and problem part (75% weight), a qualification equal to or greater than 4 out of 10 is required. Active participation in class activities contributes 10% to the final grade. Completion of laboratory practicals and submission of a final report contributes 15% to the final grade. The same evaluation criteria will be used in the extraordinary resit call.
